title.narrative: PforR on Modernization and Optimization of Public Administration

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to improve efficiency in public sector employment and finances. In this context, efficiency is the reduction in the cost of doing government business. This will be achieved by addressing systemic weaknesses in the allocation of employees and their remuneration, streamlining and rationalizing public procurement and strengthening controls over public expendiure.

The objective of the Modernization and Optimization of Public Administration Program Project for Serbia is to improve efficiency in public sector employment and finances. The Government of Serbia has launched an ambitious program of public sector reforms that seek to enhance efficiency in the public sector. The Government's overall framework for reforming public sector administration is set out in a (PAR Strategy adopted in 2014. Together with the action plan for the Implementation of the Public Sector Reform Strategy (2015-2017), adopted in 2015, the strategy sets out the immediate priorities of the Government of Serbia with respect to key reforms in the public administration. Both the PAR Strategy and Action Plan cover five major areas of reform: improvement of the organization and functioning of the public administration systems; strengthening of human resource management; improvement of public finance and public procurement management; increased transparency and enhancement of ethical standards and strengthening the Government's supervision capacities. The PAR strategy complements and incorporates elements of other strategic planning instruments, notably the Procurement Strategy (2014), the Public Financial Management Reform Program (2015) and the Action Plan for Open Government Partnership (2014). The Bank's engagement supports these reforms in the core systems of human resource management, public financial management and public procurement. These reforms are addressed in turn below with a focus on human resource management, in many respects the most challenging part of the reform agenda.

title.narrative: Share of public administration employees assigned to new pay grades as per the Law on Public Sector Employees Salary System

comment.narrative: <p>Not achieved. Achievement of this result is associated with the full implementation of the new wage system outlined in the Law on Public Sector Employees Salary System. Given that the GoS decided to postpone the full implementation of this law to 2021, the target was not achieved.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Not achieved. The Government decided to postpone implementation of the Law on Public Sector Employees Salary System to 2021.</p>

title.narrative: Ministries with retrenchment plans, identifying redundant positions

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Based on the information provided by the MPALSG, no new retrenchment plans were required or adopted in 2018. All required retrenchment plans were adopted in the previous year.</p>

title.narrative: Indirect Budget Beneficiaries included in the FMIS

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The MoF communicated that by December 31, 2018 an additional group of indirect budget beneficiaries (IBBs) comprising social institutions, were included in the budget execution system, increasing the number from 318 to 529, achieving the program target of 526 IBBs fully.</p>

<p>Achieved. The targets were consistently exceeded over the years.</p>

<p>2016: 3,288 certified in total (target - 2000)</p>

<p>2017: 3,762 certified in total (target - 2200)</p>

<p>2018: 4,236 certified in total (target 2400)</p>

<p>2019: 4,727 certified in total</p>

<p>Not achieved. However, the Budget Inspection unit has undergone restructuring, upgrading, and strengthening. The number of inspections completed in 2018 was 15. In December 2018, the budget inspectorate was elevated from a unit within a sector to a separate sector, and the number of employees was increased to 19.</p>

title.narrative: Public procurement contracts awarded through framework agreements for all contracting authorities

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. In 2018, 35,862 contracts were awarded through Framework Agreements, far exceeding the set target.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of commitments in budget execution system entered within the required deadline per the Law on Deadline for Payments in Commercial Transactions

comment.narrative: <p>With the establishment of the Central Register of Invoices in the Treasury Administration, as of March 2018, the target was achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Share of public procurement contracts within the category of public authorities over 5,000,000 RSD in value, signed in a Fiscal Year of the Borrower, in 90 days or less between the date of Issuance o

comment.narrative: <p>The targets were consistently exceeded over the years, and the final target (i.e. the target for 2018) was also exceeded.</p>

title.narrative: Employee Registry functioning according to defined criteria in the Law on Registry of all Employees, Elected, Nominated, Appointed, and Engaged Persons within Public Funds Beneficiaries

comment.narrative: <p>Not achieved. Although the main Registry in the Treasury Administration is operational, it is not fully compliant in terms of sending regular updates to the employee registry for public sector entities.</p>

title.narrative: At least 70% of public administration employee positions assigned to new pay grades according to the Law on Public Sector Employees Salary System

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved in December 2017 after the approval of two laws:  Amendments to the Law of the Salary System of Public Sector Employees and the Law on Employees in the Public Services.</p>
